Let the two ends of a wire be \(P\) and \(Q\).

1. If the corresponding ends of an identical copy were joined to \(P\) and \(Q\) respectively, the copy would have to lie directly on top of the original, which is not allowed.

For Wire D, assign coordinates to its two lower tips as
\[
P=(1,0),\qquad Q=(2,0).
\]
Tracing the wire gives
\[
(1,0)\to(1,1)\to(0,1)\to(0,2)\to(3,2)\to(3,1)\to(2,1)\to(2,0).
\]
A half-turn about the midpoint \((3/2,0)\) sends this arc to
\[
(2,0)\to(2,-1)\to(3,-1)\to(3,-2)\to(0,-2)\to(0,-1)\to(1,-1)\to(1,0).
\]
The original lies above the line \(PQ\), while the rotated copy lies below it. Hence they meet only at \(P\) and \(Q\), producing one closed shape with no crossings or other contacts.
